rows.text: Yes, that's us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Thank goodness... I hear you're both exceptional warriors as masterful as the Chrysos Heirs. Could you help us restore this column here?
rows.speaker: Disturbed Resident

rows.text: Nothing has been going right these days. First those minions of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} attack, and now this column collapses right outside our home... Can we really keep going?
rows.speaker: Disturbed Resident

rows.text: Restore it...? With just human effort, that's going to take a couple of days, at least.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not with human effort, of course, silly!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: High Priest Tribbie! O {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} on high, our prayers are heard! We won't need to trouble you any further, kind warriors.
rows.speaker: Disturbed Resident

rows.text: Oh... He thought we could summon miracles.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Eh? When we all arrived in Okhema? Come to think of it, we felt something a bit odd, too.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Eh? You can recite this, too? Wait, did you also chant this when we arrived in Okhema?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: You move to the left. How wondrous — You've only moved a few centimeters, but the water around you has become distinctly warmer.
Maybe... you also have the ability to learn Oronyx's prayers, too?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Is that rare?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You move to the left. How wondrous — You've only moved a few centimeters, but the water around you has become distinctly warmer.
Not at all! We have lots of priests here, but some are more gifted than others.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Why don't you both try chanting? Tribbie will see if you get it!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I don't seem to be cut out for this.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Really? That's pretty impressive!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Alrighty, as long as things are going well!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: You know, we are pretty certain there's more to your sudden... arrival to Okhema. And Tribbie has never seen a priest achieve resonance with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} on their first try.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Yeah! We knew it, there are also Janusopolis priests beyond the sk — um, beyond Okhema... like the city you're from!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Not if it's just the two of you. But if any of the Council Elders happen to ask... it's our little secret~!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Hmm? Were you expecting otherwise...?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We know, right? Aren't Titans amazing?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Okay, time to get back to work. Have fun exploring the city! We'll see you two later!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Look, someone's on the roof.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That should be a good vantage point to photograph the city. Let's find a way up.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: An excellent lookout over the city. We can even see that Titan statue. Let's get a photo of this view.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Relay the information obtained from Aglaea and the agreement reached with her to Dan Heng...
What are you two doing up here?
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: I know you. You're the heroes who helped defend our city, right? I, Damionis, saw your valiant figures in the battle.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Nice to meet you. We're... soldiers from a faraway city.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's our first time in Okhema, so we thought we'd find a nice vantage point to... uh, create...? No, capture...? I mean, to remember this city and its sights by.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh... You mean to say "take a photo," don't you?
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Ahem, yes. I meant to say that.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Aha! You met the right person! The name's Damionis, and I may have some humble insight on travel and photography... After all, everyone in this holy city knows me as the explorer!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Alright, pass me your photostone.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: ...I'm not even going to bother guessing their logic for naming things.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, this is an entirely foreign make. But that's not going to stop me! I'm guessing this here... and that... Hah! Easy-peasy, I know how to use this now.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: ...It's no biggie! Okay, strike your poses and look this way!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: And... we're done! Here, have a look!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Not bad.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Don't be so nitpicky.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Let's leave that to March.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Heh, as long as you're happy with the photos.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Say, I've been wanting to ask you guys something. I didn't think I'd actually get the chance but...
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: You're... You're not really from another city, are you?
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: I don't think I understand your question.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've heard some things here and there. Refugees that just came into the city are saying that the people Lord Phainon picked up are from beyond the sky.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Sorry to disappoint you, sir. I'm afraid those rumors are just rumors.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We're from Thalassopolis, a sparsely populated frontier village. Our journey to the holy city was fraught with challenges but thankfully, we were able to make our way here after meeting Phainon at the Abyss.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Thalassopolis...?
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Oh, is that so... I... I'd thought that I had finally found proof that a world beyond the sky exists.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: ...Hey, remember the agreement.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Haha, it doesn't matter! At any rate, thanks for your help, warriors of Thalassopolis.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Okhema welcomes you.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: That was close, but I have a bad feeling about this.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't think that we managed to fool him.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: After all, Thalassopolis was something I came up with on the fly. If he's truly an explorer familiar with the geography of Amphoreus, I'm afraid that he'll have already seen through our lies.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Fortunately, there's no evidence. But... seems like even though the starry sky is taboo on Amphoreus, there are people who still yearn for it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Looks like we have to be even more cautious.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Where should we go next?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Right, we were going to explore the city before we got distracted.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Look, Phainon is over there.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Out of the shadow of the past, you've not stepped, Chrysos Heir.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: The weight of the Coreflame, if you wish to bear... You must bury the past, suspend the pain.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: I'll try my best, Chartonus. But why keep mentioning it if you already know I can't do it?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You stare intently at the red clay in your hand, then look up to check the dromas' expression.
Grumphhh... Grumphhh!
rows.speaker: Dromas

rows.text: Grumphhh... Grumphhh!
rows.speaker: Dromas

rows.text: ...Here, your guests are.
rows.speaker: Chartonus

rows.text: [Trailblazer], Dan Heng! You're back much quicker than I imagined. I thought that Aglaea would keep you for a bit longer.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Here you go. This is the compensation I previously mentioned. I asked the most famous Grand Craftsman in the holy city to repair your spear.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Once again, let me offer my sincere apologies for any offense I caused during our first meeting.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Judging solely from its exterior, I cannot see any signs of damage. It's truly incredible.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The one who crafted this spear must also be a renowned master. I guess there's always someone greater out there. Although I still can't imagine a world outside Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You could say she's not very talkative? No, that's not it, she's just a little elusive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You could say she's not very talkative? No, that's not it, she's just a little elusive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Or perhaps I've just never given it much thought until I met you two.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You've probably now heard about the tripartite prophecy that descended upon Amphoreus and the mission of the Chrysos Heirs. For us, pursuing the prophecy is the purpose of our journey. Therefore, thinking too much about other things is unnecessary.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's considered a prophecy because it manifested as a miracle, though its origin or whose will it represents remains unknown.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There's another theory that it is the whispers of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} before their eternal slumber. It was the sky father who scattered their divine blood all over the land that gave rise to the Chrysos Heirs... Of course, this is just one of many popular folktales.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Please don't simply dismiss it as silly superstition. The people of this world have already experienced the transition from skepticism to firm belief, and this transition wasn't easy to achieve. Many have paid the price.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What Aglaea conveyed to us was more of a collective mission. As an individual, what role do you play in all of this, Phainon?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Me? I'm still seeking that answer myself.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But if the gods favor me, I believe that my Coreflame won't be far.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'm a soldier who was taught how to fight at a young age. From the day I was selected by the prophecy, I've regarded {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}the Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#} as my goal.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: One day, I'll break the lance and take the Coreflame of Strife.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...But discussing such a bitter topic is a bummer. I'm embarrassed since I think I'm the one who brought it up.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Oh right, Tribbie mentioned that you two also use teleslates. Why don't we exchange contacts? Please also accept these gifts as a token of my appreciation.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Since the weather is great, why don't you two look around some more? I won't take up more of your time. See you later.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hey, that's... the lady we encountered previously.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ah... It's our two distinguished guests.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Welcome to the dwelling of the dromases... Well, I'm also just passing by.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Really? I find it rather sweet... It's the fragrance of life.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes. I enjoy the air here. It's rather sweet... Full of the fragrance of life.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Speaking of which, is Miss Castorice also a Chrysos Heir?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...My apologies. If you don't wish to talk about this topic, I'll stop myself here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Thank you, Mr. Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...No, thank you. Unless you wish to make things worse.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...It seems to have understood you, but it's choosing to ignore you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Their feed is dry redsoil and it's very clean. There is some over there.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Since it's your first time feeding, just a small piece will do.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Of course, but it's very bitter and hard to digest.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Grab the crystallized dry redsoil.
...That's not going to happen.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It looks very happy. Perhaps... you could try petting it?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It seems to enjoy it a lot. You get along very well with the dromas.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It makes me envious.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Me? No, thanks. It's alright...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Miss Castorice, are you concerned about something? Since we've just arrived in this area, we hope to build closer relationships with everyone through our actions.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Please don't misunderstand. When you helped Okhema, you already showed ample goodwill. It's just that I...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...am not too good with social "contact." Regardless of whether it's with people or with these children.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So, please don't take it to heart.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Alright. [Trailblazer], take a photo of the dromas as well. It's rare to encounter such an amazing creature.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Would you two like a photo with this child? In that case, I might be able to help.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes, it is an interest of mine.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's not it. Photography is an interest of mine.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Alright then. Thanks for your help.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No problem. Please place the photostone on the ground.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Let's just do as she says.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What beautiful colors. It's... very cute.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The aperture, exposure index, and preset filter... Although it looks different on the outside, it actually has the same internal structure. There won't be any issues.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Alright, get into position.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And we're done. I hope that you like it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...But, what's the reason behind using the black and white filter?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ah... My apologies, it's just personal preference. I like black and white photos. If it bothers you, I can take another photo.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That won't be necessary. This is fine.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm glad that I could help.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then, I'll take my leave now. Please continue playing with the dromases.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Why are you speaking like a Stellaron Hunter all of a sudden?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You could say Miss Castorice is not very talkative? No, that's not it, she's just a little elusive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Even when we came across her previously, she avoided having physical contact with others...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: These Chrysos Heirs all have wildly different personalities. In comparison, Phainon seems like the most normal one.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Should we return to Marmoreal Palace? Or do you want to wander around for a bit more?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ma'am, this item of yours is new! Completely new! There's no doubt about it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: T—That's impossible! This is an heirloom that's been passed down by my ancestors... Where's Theodoros? Get him over here to take a look!
rows.speaker: Elderly Appraiser

rows.text: Although I'm not as experienced at doing appraisals as he is, I'm very confident about this. If you don't trust me, you can take it elsewhere for a second opinion.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Or, I can burn it for you? You'll be able to tell once you smell it!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: N—No way! You can't burn my family heirloom!
rows.speaker: Elderly Appraiser

rows.text: I never thought that Phainon had such a hobby...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: He seems to be dealing with someone difficult right now. Let's leave him to it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...The strife of day and night birthed the all-knowing giant. Their feet measure the earth and their back carries the dawn and dusk.
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: With the night as their curtain, they dreamt until they awoke. Only then did they realize: My perfection was born for creation.
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: Gods, please hear my wish:
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: Craft my likeness with fresh earth, and grant my intellect with your fruits. Illuminate my emotions with the wings of a butterfly and forge my fate with golden blood.
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: The perfect gods created the very first humans, and the first humans created the first city.
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: Okhema! Standing at the foot of the {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Throne of Worlds{RUBY_E#}, your golden blood can be traced back to the very beginning.
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: Though the black tide devours the ancient lands, the holy city will cross over to a new world...
rows.speaker: Bard

rows.text: Hey, are you in the forum?
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: Forum? Which one?
rows.speaker: Bored Citizen

rows.text: The one about the Rosy Celestial Maiden. Its getting more popular by the minute! I don't see you in there yet. Hurry up! It's filling up quickly.
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: "Why should I trust you?" That was your immediate response. However, you and Dan Heng need to build good relationships with the locals to complete your trailblazing journey.
"At least cooperate for now and try to earn her trust," you persuade yourself.
You feel your cheeks warm up and quickly switch hands.
Rosy Celestial Maiden, forum...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I have a strange feeling about this. I hope that it's not what I think it is... Let's go take a look.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Excuse me, we accidentally overheard something about a forum just now... We would like to find out more.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hmm? Your outfits, who exactly...
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: We're warriors from a foreign land who assisted in the defense of Okhema.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ah, brave warriors, pardon me! I didn't expect you to be interested in such social affairs, but sure thing.
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: Please take out your teleslate. I'll help you connect to Okhema's World Wound Web.
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: Got it! Please take a look!
rows.speaker: Charming Citizen

rows.text: Oh no!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer] & Dan Heng

rows.text: That Damionis guy who took a photo for us... It must be him! He must have opened the album and saw the photos that March 7th previously took.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's beside the point.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There are more than a hundred people in here. Although no one believes what Damionis is saying now, we don't know what he'll do next. If the situation gets out of control, the consequences might be disastrous.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Quick! We have to find Damionis before things get worse.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There are so many people all of a sudden...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: At a time like this... Why not ask around?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Rosy Celestial Maiden, just from this name alone am I able to imagine your beauty! You must be the incarnation of {RUBY_B#Romance Titan}Mnestia{RUBY_E#}. You cause me to sink deeper and deeper, unable to get a hold of myself...
rows.speaker: Romantic Citizen

rows.text: Oh, beautiful celestial maiden, how can I ever win your affection?
rows.speaker: Romantic Citizen

rows.text: ... Is March 7th really that simple in your eyes?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's get to the point.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dameas? Aminos? No, I don't know what you're talking about, friend...
rows.speaker: Romantic Citizen

rows.text: Right now, I only have the Rosy Celestial Maiden in my heart!
rows.speaker: Romantic Citizen

rows.text: Wonder what he drank. Someone should come calm him down.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's go and look elsewhere.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, Rosy Celestial Maiden... You truly are a gift from the heavens, a daughter of the sun!
rows.speaker: Dashing Citizen

rows.text: Even {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#} cannot restrain you. Will you gently carve open the sky? If only to lead us out of this long dark night...
rows.speaker: Dashing Citizen

rows.text: ...Hey.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Who? No. I do not care about any Damionis. Right now...
rows.speaker: Dashing Citizen

rows.text: ...I only have beautiful fantasies and poems in my heart! Oh, Rosy Celestial Maiden, the light of Okhema...
rows.speaker: Dashing Citizen

rows.text: ...Next.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dear citizens, please stop spreading images of unknown origins!
rows.speaker: Sensible Citizen

rows.text: You give March 7th's camera to Damionis...

Please wake up! The Rosy Celestial Maiden is a lie crafted by {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#} as a prank. We should follow the lead of Lady Aglaea and not subject ourselves to such mind-numbing fantasies...
rows.speaker: Sensible Citizen

rows.text: Don't stir up trouble.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Damionis? That explorer who thinks very highly of himself?
rows.speaker: Sensible Citizen

rows.text: I've heard of him but have never met him in person. Others have said that he's completely crazy—
rows.speaker: Sensible Citizen

rows.text: What's that commotion?
rows.speaker: Sensible Citizen

rows.text: He's running toward the Garden of Life. Give chase!
rows.speaker: Holy City Guard

rows.text: Citizen! Calm down. Don't do anything foolish!
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: This is the Garden of Life, the holy ground of the {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Bough of Rift{RUBY_E#}! Are you trying to defile the gods?
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: Defile the gods? No, you guys are completely wrong! The wise {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} will be proud of me. Just watch!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: What is he trying to do? Let's get closer and take a look.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The wisdom of {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} should be shared equally by all.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: I, Explorer Damionis, shall put on these wings today and touch the sky — proving to everyone that a world beyond the sky exists!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Damionis left thoughtfully.
...Wings?
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: That's right — right here, right now!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: That is a giant Flying Amphora. You're going to fall to your death!
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: Heh, ridicule me all you want. I shall prove myself and remove all doubts!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Obviously not.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We can't stand by and watch him die. Let's go.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You two are... the distinguished guests of Lady Aglaea?
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: Mr. Damionis, please calm down. Don't act rashly.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...My dear friends, I know that you must have your own reasons to hide the truth. I shall not make things difficult for you.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: But thank you for showing me the image from beyond the sky. Now, I shall embark on this earthshaking undertaking — Damionis always follows through on his words!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Save your words of persuasion. I've made up my mind.
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Since appeasing him did not work, it's time for a change in strategy.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Haha, my friend, your tone has betrayed you! I understand that you're trying to persuade me to stay...
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Haha, trying to enrage me in hopes that my emotions will overwhelm my mission? It's... It's a pity that I've seen through your intentions. You're... You're trying to persuade me to stay...
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: A clever fool. That's how to describe people like him, right?
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: I'm almost moved by his persistence...
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: Save your words. {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}, feel my wrath!
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: We're running out of time...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's a human life after all! There's no choice. Let's just tell him...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What... did you just say?
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: So... I was right? You really are from... beyond the sky?
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: ...We are bound by a pact. I cannot reveal the truth to you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A pact? Ah, so that's why he called you "distinguished guests of Aglaea"...
rows.speaker: Damionis

rows.text: Damionis! We're taking you in for an interrogation!
rows.speaker: Impulsive Guard

rows.text: This is not going to go well.
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: What will happen to Damionis?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: He learned something that he should never have learned. We can only hand him over to Lady Aglaea for judgment.
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: Instead of worrying about his safety, perhaps you guys should worry about the impact of the rumors. Although no one believes what Damionis said about a world beyond the sky, the Rosy Celestial Maiden has already spread everywhere.
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: ...We're sorry for the trouble that we caused.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's alright. I think there's only one thing you can do right now. Go to Verax Leo and share something even more interesting with him. That way, there's a chance that you can cover up the rumors.
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: As for what happened earlier... We won't tell anyone else about it. So, go now, brave heroes.
rows.speaker: Kind Guard

rows.text: Grumph... Grumphhh!
rows.speaker: Dromas

rows.text: Grumphhhh... Grumphhh!
rows.speaker: Dromas

rows.text: The big guy in front lets out a satisfied sound.
You don't know how it chews and digests these clumps of clay — but to them, these hard red clays must be as delicious as a freshly sizzling steak.
Grumphhh!
rows.speaker: Dromas

rows.text: This is going to be difficult. Let's try to salvage the situation before Aglaea finds out...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What's this? It looks like one of those mannequins in the clothing stores of Penacony.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's also a... butterfly? Is that a fashion accessory?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...How intriguing.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But I noticed a sense of unease in Castorice. She trusted in them and even reached out to Phainon in secret, believing I was unaware...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Therefore, I took advantage of the situation and changed the threat from "banishment" to "execution," to see if the two could remain firm under the most extreme pressure.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Simultaneously, it might also strengthen their bonds with Phainon and Castorice.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Do you have to go to such lengths for the battle against {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: That's going to make it a lot tougher for you to gain their trust...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: That's not important.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You and I will eventually step off the stage and leave Amphoreus' fate in the hands of others... That's the future you foresee, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Yeah.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: All four questions have been asked and answered.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The prophecy of deliverance is nothing if not ambiguous. It urges us to defy the gods yet refrains from providing a clear glimpse of what lies ahead.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Right now, it is people's faith in the prophecy that unites them around the Chrysos Heirs. Should a time come when their faith is shaken... all will crumble.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hence, we must be prepared. When our task is to craft the armor for the Deliverer, what harm is there if you and I don humble attire?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Agy... Have you noticed...
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Regardless of your choice, the Chrysos Heirs will continue to follow the path in the prophecy.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You keep saying that you don't believe in humanity's altruism, but your actions are a counterexample.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Perhaps it's because my "humanity" is distancing itself from me.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Another never-ending dawn. How bright is the day, and how long is the night.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Things don't have to end on a sour note between us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The golden thread hangs unusually silent today, as if the heavens, earth, and ocean are all holding their breath. Could they be mourning the impending downfall of a Titan...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Unwinding in a bath sounds appealing now... Would you care to join me?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Phainon?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Let's go, Agy. When have we ever been able to say no in all these hundreds of years?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Do speak your mind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: When I first met them in the Abyss, I was wary of them as well and never let my guard down throughout our journey back to the holy city.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: However, during the battle to defend Okhema, we fought side by side numerous times. The look in someone's eyes in moments of life-and-death never lies, and I was able to detect the conviction in their eyes back then. That's why I was willing to put my life in their hands.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Please believe a warrior's intuition.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: At present, Okhema is desperate for aid, and I am loath to lose two allies just like that.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Isn't this what Miss Castorice believes as well?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Yeah.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm more willing to view "death" as a peaceful farewell than a punishment.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So, two Chrysos Heirs are willing to vouch for you. Hah... It seems my actions were too high-handed.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon, will you fulfill your duty as host and look after our distinguished guests?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: While I'm not good at formalities, I'll do my best.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Cas... Next time, I hope you will express your thoughts openly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I will.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Now, it's time to welcome the newcomers to the Vortex of Genesis. As you both have chosen to trust these outlanders, ensure they are adequately informed about the mysteries concealed within.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: All four questions have been asked and answered.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Mmm... What's that sound?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Sound? Who? That? Which?
Who's talking...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Calm down. Calm down. This time. Next time?
Castorice places her slender, pale finger over your pulse.
A chill seeps through your skin, then immediately spreads into your veins.
Castorice adds a second finger... then a third, until half her palm gently envelops your left wrist.
A subtle fragrance of an unnamed flower fills your senses, its sweetness making you forget the need to breathe.
Your vision blurs, and cold reality fades into a purple ocean — her promised land of flowers.
Then, you finally understand...
...you are currently welcoming your own sweet demise.
...Who? Who is? You... I... Who am I?
...Phainon?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Ron? Stella? Who? You... I... Who am I?
Do speak your mind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: When I first met them in the Abyss, I was wary of them as well and never let my guard down throughout our journey back to the holy city.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: However, during the battle to defend Okhema, we fought side by side numerous times. The look in someone's eyes in moments of life-and-death never lies, and I was able to detect the conviction in their eyes back then. That's why I was willing to put my life in their hands.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Please believe a warrior's intuition.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: At present, Okhema is desperate for aid, and I am loath to lose two allies just like that.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Isn't this what Miss Castorice believes as well?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Yeah.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm more willing to view "death" as a peaceful farewell than a punishment.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Sleep? Here? There? You... I... Who am I?
So, two Chrysos Heirs are willing to vouch for you. Hah... It seems my actions were too high-handed.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon, will you fulfill your duty as host and look after our distinguished guests?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: While I'm not good at formalities, I'll do my best.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Cas... Next time, I hope you will express your thoughts openly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I will.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Now, it's time to welcome the newcomers to the Vortex of Genesis. As you both have chosen to trust these outlanders, ensure they are adequately informed about the mysteries concealed within.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Broken. Lost. Want... complete.
...Sleep. Go sleep. Disturb... should not.
Things don't have to end on a sour note between us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Regardless of your choice, the Chrysos Heirs will continue to follow the path in the prophecy.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: (Am I... dreaming?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: In the meantime...
(Feels like there's been a voice talking in my head all night...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I should probably mention this to Dan Heng.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Did you already forget? The sky has been this bright since we arrived at the holy city.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes, I wake up easily when it's too bright outside... The sky has been like this since we arrived at the holy city.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Did you sleep well?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A voice? The Voice of the Stellaron again or...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That sounds a bit contradictory.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: In a way, chaos is the nature of dreams.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So, it wasn't a nightmare. But be careful, that might be its means of luring you in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Keep a note of whatever you can remember. This strange dream might be connected to the rules of this world.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yes. In the worst case, the entrance to Amphoreus is a one-way door, letting people in but not out.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I wasn't expecting the expedition to set off after only a night of rest.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's set the questions aside for now. The Chrysos Heirs are getting ready to mobilize.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Great to see you here!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph... Entrusting our fates to two strangers, is this madness or folly?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Maybe both. You should really make more friends, Mydei.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Heroes, your attention please.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Trianne has returned with news: For the first time in many years, we have dispersed the fog around Castrum Kremnos and verified its location.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The awaited moment has finally arrived for the Chrysos Heirs. Our path forward is now clear: Vanquish {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, the violent Lance of Fury, and bring the Coreflame of Strife back to Okhema to fuel the prophesized miracle.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: This is an arduous mission, and I must heed the voices of all to determine the best candidates for this campaign.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Should you harbor any thoughts, this is the moment to bring them forth.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, wish to join the crusade against {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Furthermore, I recommend the two warriors from foreign lands. They have fought alongside me against {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s double, and I have full faith in their bravery.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Lounging in a bath chamber isn't exactly trailblazing.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are you still not used to it? This is the destiny of a Trailblazer.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I, Mydei from Castrum Kremnos, volunteer to join.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} has become corrupted over the years, their pride waning, but their might endures. Victory only lies in assembling a full-fledged army.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...I'm willing to join as well, to help guide departing souls and ease everyone's burdens...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I concur with your opinion. Though their divinity has faded, {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} remains a formidable adversary.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Yet, I cannot jeopardize all of your lives in one single battle.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: As we speak, the {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Hand of Shadow{RUBY_E#} remains missing, the {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Eye of Twilight{RUBY_E#} is still coveting our land, and {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} present significant threats, despite their lack of overt hostility toward humanity.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Even with two demigods protecting the holy city, the risk is too great. Hence...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Castorice, you must remain here. Your place is not on the front lines, and the battlefield is best left to the warriors.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...I understand.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: As for the two foreign warriors... Select one to accompany you, Phainon. Placing both esteemed guests on the front line would not be proper.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: [Trailblazer] excels in wielding a range of weapons, and {M#his}{F#her} flaming lance has quelled the enemy's advances multiple times. Mydei and I are both better at offense, so from a tactical standpoint...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: [Trailblazer], would you be willing to fight alongside us?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: With those two, the battle should end quickly.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What are you talking about? Now's not the time for jokes.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If [Trailblazer] has no objections... Aglaea, the three of us will take on the mission to hunt down the Titan.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Mydeimos, Castrum Kremnos was your home. Your people were once {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} followers, yet you've chosen to turn to Okhema and dedicate yourself to the prophecy.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Do you swear upon {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s body to make this mission of the Chrysos Heirs your foremost duty?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: When {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} succumbed to madness, they stopped being a god to my people.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I will use my wrath as a human to strip that god of their authority. As for the Coreflame and that soon-to-be-vacant divine throne...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: If that is the object you desire, you can have it. I have no interest in becoming a replacement god.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hah! How generous, but I'm not the type to accept charity, so I'll definitely be the one who deals the final blow through {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s heart.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The party that will embark on the expedition to Castrum Kremnos is decided: Phainon from Aedes Elysiae, Mydei from Castrum Kremnos, and... [Trailblazer] from the outlands.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I — Aglaea from Okhema, Chrysos Heir and the demigod who bears {RUBY_B#Romance Titan}Mnestia{RUBY_E#}'s divine authority — hereby bless your journey ahead.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Trianne will open the gate that will lead you to Castrum Kremnos. May the golden thread guide you on your journey and bring you safely home.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I plan to stay here for a while and learn more about Amphoreus from Lady Tribbie. You'll handle the action, and I'll deal with the research. We each have a role to play.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Shall we have a goodbye hug?
Please, come back victorious.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'll pray for you. May your steps be ever quicker than death's relentless pursuit.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It is by the will of the gods that you stood on Okhema's side in the end.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I thought you didn't trust me.
No thanks to you.
You are Phainon and Mydei's companion. So long as they're willing to entrust you with their lives, my trust in you doesn't matter.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Go. Stand with the two Chrysos Heirs. Okhema has need of a true god of war. It's time for the mad god {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} reign to end.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hahaha, were you expecting actual city gates?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's true Trianne is very playful, but she's the best gatekeeper in Amphoreus. Her Century Gate never fails.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Instead of worrying about gates, why don't you take the time to think about how the three of us are supposed to fend off an entire army.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Slay, slay!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Keep yourself safe, and work within your capabilities.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Get ready! Get ready! I don't wanna wait! Slowpoke!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: It's quieter than I expected...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's corrupted... but still familiar.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This is Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Times really have changed. Even {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} own lands are on the verge of collapse. I haven't seen any sign of Titankin.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If even half of Castrum Kremnos' old might remains, it would mean that Aglaea sent us to our deaths.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This is the outer city corridor. It used to be heavily guarded by soldiers. Even with the two of us working together, we wouldn't have made it past thirty steps.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Think whatever you want.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Yeah, Kremnos used to be the place every warrior longed for.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Kind of a shame you didn't live in that era full of strong warriors, eh Mydei? If all the heroes of the past hadn't fallen one after another, I wouldn't be the only worthy opponent you have left.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are you scared? It's still not too late to run.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: No, I'm just thinking about the warriors who also braved this very corridor in the past. They all ventured towards the city of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}the Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#}, all just to set their names in gold.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The fortress may be in ruins now, but what we're about to do is no different from what they were striving for back then.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's go. We'll take back the Coreflame of Strife or die in Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Those are the only two paths to glory we can choose from.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Trianne, the road ahead is dangerous. You should stay here and find a safe place to hide.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We'll return once we complete our mission. Then we'll have to trouble you to use the Century Gate again, alright?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Got it. Hide so the baddies can't find me!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Is she really a demigod...
She still looks and acts just like a child.
Trianne has sacrificed a lot for Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: By the way, aren't you going to tell [Trailblazer] any stories about Castrum Kremnos? Aren't you worried I'll tell {M#him}{F#her} all the historical myths you despise?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So... you'll end things here? Are you sure about that?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: How does it feel to be home again after so long?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not here. I lived in the inner city.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Oh... As befitting of the crown prince of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I'd like to see you try.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: *sigh* It's exhausting talking to you sometimes...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Tell me about this one.
Is this Tetris?
Castrum Kremnos has been {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s territory since ancient times. It's a massive moving fortress that surrounds the Titan, built by their followers.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In the age before the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#} fell from grace, Castrum Kremnos would follow the Lance into battle after battle. It's a city that enforces strict discipline and reveres military might.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Compared to that, the customs of my home feel very unsophisticated.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There. Once we pass through that gate, we'll be in the acropolis.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: We'll finally see some soldiers roaming about.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How's it going? You look stumped. I'll be going on ahead though.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Mere lightning won't stop a warrior of Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: They're minions who've succumbed to depravity. Smashing them to pieces would be the greatest mercy.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It seems enemies aren't the only things stopping us. This bridge has fallen into disrepair. I suppose even Kremnoan craftsmanship can be unreliable sometimes.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Sorry to disappoint, but the outer city was built by convicts.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: No wonder it's so fragile. Maybe these people were taking their grievances out on you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Doesn't matter. There's no shame in resistance here, whether it's from an adversary or a convict on death row.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Except now, it's stopping the people trying to kill {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}. It's moments like this that make me miss Tribbie's power.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But since you've volunteered, please be my guest.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look, the gate opened—
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Genius. We never would have known if you hadn't said anything.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let's go. We can take a detour from the broken bridge.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look, in the sky! That's...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Blade of Fury — Even if the world lay shattered, it would still hang high above everyone's heads.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It's magnificent...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You haven't seen it at its most magnificent.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's the giant sword {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} used to destroy {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila's{RUBY_E#} heavenly kingdom long ago, followed by one city-state after another.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It's not just a weapon, it's the faith of the Kremnoan people. Souls who died heroically on the battlefield will further temper the blade in {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s hand, becoming a part of the god-king's power.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Such is the Titan's conquest — {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, the Titankin, and the people who have faith in Strife sweep away all their enemies. Even in death, they embrace eternal glory.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I think you're exaggerating a little. I can think of at least three losses suffered by Castrum Kremnos in the Chrysos War, just off the top of my head.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There's no shame in losing to those who conspire and plot in secret. Those weak and despicable individuals are the ones who should be ashamed.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: True. Valorous Death Before Glorious Return. The Kremnoan people have always been straightforward. They spend their whole lives running to the battlefield. No wonder {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#} loves teasing you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...But that's all in the past.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Guess what I'm thinking, Mydei?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Probably nothing good. Keep it simple.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This isn't just an expedition. It's also a battle to determine a victor. Since we're already here, why don't we have a match and fight to our heart's content?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Just you and me. Let's recreate the original Kremnos Festival.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Show me what the grandest fighting competition in Castrum Kremnos was like. Let's gild this expedition with another layer of glory and compete to see who can kill the most crazed Titankin. How about it?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What's the prize?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The privilege of delivering the final blow to {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Interesting. I accept your challenge.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I know Mydei. He prefers to fight alone. There are two paths ahead. [Trailblazer] and I will take the same one.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A faint murmur rides the wind — a whisper of ancient history, the elegy of God...
...and the rumble of Strife.
Doesn't matter to me even if you do.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You don't know the lay of the land, so I'll give you a ten-step head start.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Haha! He already thinks he's won, but I won't decline the offer either. Let's get going, [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Why are you still standing there?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Returning the favor. Ten steps are too many, you can have one back.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Made it! Hopefully the enemies on this side are worthy of our combined might.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We fought them together, so naturally I can only take half the credit. That's what I call fair play.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry. Mydei is strong, and so am I.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Why are you just standing there? Giving up already?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Whoa... That's impressive.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Following an iron chain, onto the path leading to the giant sword on the other side? This is more like it!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Huh? When did you get over there?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I told you before that you don't know the lay of the land in this city. That's why you won't beat me.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: And just so you know: I'm at six.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Wow, seems like luck is on your side. Our path was a little lax on security. Not to worry though, I'll catch up once we cross this iron chain bridge.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Assuming you can get across. Do you see the lightning bolts striking the chain?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It doesn't look like ordinary lightning, which means mindlessly running across would spell certain death.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There happens to be a Prophecy Tablet here though. Let's go take a look. Maybe it'll help us.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Whoa! You're nimbler than I thought!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Worry about yourself. There's an endless abyss below us.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: —That's more like it!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You practically have nine lives and, on top of that, you're lucky? I'm almost jealous.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Whew... That was a close one. Thankfully we both have a remarkable sense of balance.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So, this is a lounge? It feels out of place.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Maybe this is where all the warriors in the past took their breaks during competitions.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hm... Just regular old bits and pieces. Nothing that stands out.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There's a thick layer of dust. Guess no one's been here for a long time. They must have been left behind by Mydei's people when they departed.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Who are his people exactly?
It's hard to imagine people used to live here...
You've likely seen them in Okhema, but it's hard to tell just by appearance.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It was a city of warriors, but ordinary citizens lived here too.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They look the same as anyone else. They just have traditions that are slightly... different from ours.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry. We have an expert next door. We can show it to Mydei when we group back up.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Did Amphoreus have more dealings with worlds beyond the sky than we thought? But nothing like this was ever recorded in our historical materials.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's a gadget that records your voice. People don't like this sort of thing nowadays.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Why don't you hold on to it, [Trailblazer]? It makes a sound when you shake it. Should make for an interesting collectible.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Give you something to show for your trip, in addition to the photos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, we've turned over every nook and cranny. It's time to move on.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Wait... What's that creature doing? Is it trying to stop us?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It even killed its own comrade... They truly have no honor to speak of.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The road ahead is blocked by the iron ball...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Can you call upon {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s Miracle again?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No, that's not going to work.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Sorry, it's because I'm too weak...
Learning and mastering are two different concepts. Without a priest's resonance, an ordinary person would fall into a coma after chanting the first few words of the prayer.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Oh? Tribbie taught you how?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's definitely not my fault!
Oh? Tribbie taught you how?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's not your fault. Castrum Kremnos is {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} territory, after all. The environment is cutting off your ability to resonate with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It really isn't. Castrum Kremnos is {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} territory, after all. The environment is cutting off your ability to resonate with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In principle, there should be an instrument used by Time Priests somewhere in this fortress... Aha, there it is.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: He's both my friend and my foe. It's always been this way. Working with him always brings out my competitive side.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We've been both friends and foes since the day we met. Working with him always brings out my competitive side.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What did I tell you? I get especially lucky when I'm with you. This instrument stabilizes the connection between priests and the Three Titans of Fate. Give it a try.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There you go.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What does that mean? Alright, give it a go.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are there any side effects?
If something should happen to me...
In other words, this is our chance to overtake Mydei.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: My thoughts exactly. You have the heart of a fighter, my friend.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Relax. If something should happen to you, "I'll be sure to pass on your last words to Dan Heng, my friend!"
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: He might look honest, but he's a lot shrewder than he seems.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: He might look honest, but he's a lot shrewder than he seems.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hold your horses! We're not exactly immortal here.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "I'll be sure to pass on your last words to Dan Heng, my friend!"
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Simply put, {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#} is the Titan of trickery — thievery, deception, and betrayal, these unsavory acts are all tied to them.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry. You'll be just fine.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not bad. Something feels different about you already.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What do you propose? I'm all ears.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: There aren't any other options.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: All hail {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, my master and guide.
rows.speaker: Sculpting Zone Strong Man

rows.text: Why don't you give it another go?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: March 7th... and you think our names sound strange?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You guys mentioned her in the Vortex of Genesis earlier.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: From the sound of things, we're about to lose if we don't step it up.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yeah, I can tell.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ah, that's unfortunate.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Careful. We're getting very close to the Blade of Fury...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This is the center all right. That's a sizable formation.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If the records are correct, directly beneath the Blade of Fury lies the world-renowned Kremnos Arena. The path before us leads either to glory or to death...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Of course, glory is ours, and death is theirs!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So, that friend of yours... her name is "March"?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I must say, her name is pretty unconventional, wouldn't you agree?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You must really value your friendship with her to go through all this effort to document the journey for her.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Honestly, seeing how you both look out for your friend has furthered my trust in you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A person's true character often comes to light in their friendships. Most of what my teacher taught me has slipped away, but this sentence is still vivid in my memory.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Especially in these tumultuous times, friends who you can trust completely are a rare and precious find.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's keep going. We can't let Mydeimos get too full of himself. The Prophecy Tablet might be able to unlock that closed gate.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: According to Mydei, we need to go deeper into Castrum Kremnos. It's that way.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Maybe we can use the iron ball to smash through the roadblock. Hopefully, it leads to Castrum Kremnos' treasure vault. Otherwise, it might not be worth the effort.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But there's another exit here. I wonder where it leads.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Choose any path you like. It's entirely up to you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Blocked path? That won't stop us!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Why's the staircase blocked? Weird to think that people lived here.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well done! Go claim our rewards — no one else in Kremnos will have any use for them anyway.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: A fallen Titan, soulless kin, and a desolate fortress...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I have to say that the ability to perform miracles is innate. Without a priest's resonance, an ordinary person would fall into a coma after chanting the first few words of the prayer.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This place has fallen pretty far from the way people remember it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We meet again! What's your count so far?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Thirty.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's not too far off. We still stand a chance.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I just remembered — we came across a slate with inscriptions in an ancient language of Castrum Kremnos. Could you help translate it?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Is it beyond your knowledge, amateur historian?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Sadly, yes. You are my only hope now.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You just keep having fun. I've got better things to do.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: There's another mural up ahead. Want to take a closer look?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Looks like they're creating Titankin. Maybe this is what "Soul-Forging" means?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Crafting a body from rough stones and then infusing it with a god's golden blood to bring it to life...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No wonder Castrum Kremnos keeps winning battle after battle. With this method, they can create as many soldiers as they want...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How did you beat us here again? But there are still plenty of enemies around. What's wrong? Already tired?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I gave you two this final chance on purpose. If you're not interested, fine.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Well, how generous of you. This is the Stockpiling Zone — we must be getting close to {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's right. But by the time you arrive, he might already have fallen by my hand.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Then we must act quickly. We can't let you die right before our eyes, can we?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We won't compete on who's fastest but on the number of trophies, so we'll each be responsible for our own tally. Don't worry. I won't add {M#his}{F#her} kills to my own count.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We'll be meeting up with Mydei soon. Want to clean up this area and increase our {RUBY_B#Kremnos crest}trophy{RUBY_E#} count?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Victory or defeat, it all comes down to this, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The path is cut off. But how did he get through? Did... he set up this roadblock on purpose?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Enough joking. Let's look around...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This might come in handy — the stone table for the Hand of Zagreus. Let's use it to fill the crack in the path.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I don't normally approve of this, but given the circumstances, let's use it this one time.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We need to find a solution to mend the broken path.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ugh, not again.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This time, we might be able to use it to blow away the barrier.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So many stones here. I wonder how many war machines can be built with all this?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But after today, they'll be slumbering here forever.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This should work now. Let's just hope no more strange mechanisms get in our way.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look, someone's getting impatient.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Leo?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The sweltering heat — the Titan's wrath has set the air ablaze.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Yeah, we're getting pretty close—
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's getting even hotter. Is this place still in use?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: After we pass through here, we'll reach the Soul-Forging Zone.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The heat is unbearable, and all these thoughts are echoing in my head...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: On second thought, this could very well be where we meet our end, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Be careful. Your thoughts are being corrupted by Strife.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You're right. It was my decision to keep pushing forward. And with [Trailblazer] here, we're sure to complete our mission and return safely.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Just like the path ahead, even though it's completely dilapidated, it will still lead us to our final destination.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That Titan has fallen, but they left "Bewitching Hands" scattered all over the world. Now, people use these giant hands to move things around — and, well, to steal things, too.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let me smash it—
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Hold your horses! Don't waste your energy here — use your head.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Looks like we'll need to use the hand again.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Look out! An enemy!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Put your sword away... It seems to still be rational.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You guys mentioned her in the Vortex of Genesis earlier.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We might be able to get some clues from it.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Your ruthlessness is akin to that of the executioners in Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let me translate that for you... Actually, I'm not sure what it means either.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Ready your arms!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I've given up on figuring out the logic of these minions. They're just pure chaos.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No matter. You and I will soon bring this madness to a close.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Are you ready, Deliverer?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Always. Bearing the Coreflame of Strife... has been my deep-seated desire.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We're so close to the fall of a Titan... It feels unreal.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't think of them as a god. It's just you, me, and them — warriors in a fight to the death.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That oppressive feeling from earlier — it's back. Do you feel it, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But that bluster is no longer pure. It's mingled with the scent of blood and the cries of lost souls...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The fate I've been hoping for... lies behind this door.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The souls of war are amassing in the skies above Kremnos... surging toward the Blade of Fury!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They have no intention of winning the fight. Instead, they're using death after death to temper their blade... Even with a hundred deaths, they've resolved to pierce through {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s body!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: All their honor is gone... How did the god of our tribe fall so low?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Deliverer, here is your moment.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I'll hold them off here and keep them from wielding the Blade of Fury. You need to head back and notify the two demigods.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Are you out of your mind, facing the Titan alone? I'm staying too. [Trailblazer], please—
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Get lost! Do you have to make me say this?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I must stay here, not for Okhema's safety, but to settle the score with my god.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Even if immortality is a curse, it shouldn't be used so despicably.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Go, Deliverer. Your battlefield lies elsewhere.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Stay strong. Try not to get killed too many times.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Finally, some peace.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You and I — two warriors rejected by death. Is there any contest more fair than this?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Come forth! The king who has never claimed his throne, against the god who has fallen from grace. How perfectly matched we are!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let's battle till the world's final breath!
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: We're back.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hnngh... Tired... and dizzy... Will De be okay?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: He'll be fine... {RUBY_B#Mydei}Mydeimos{RUBY_E#} is the fiercest warrior I know.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Until our return. I'm sure of it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Go get some rest, Trianne. We might need your help again before you know it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Okay... Don't worry about me! Take care of yourselves, too...
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Let's go, [Trailblazer]... It's a race against time. We have to find Aglaea right away.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They're back.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Are you okay? Are you injured? Things didn't sound good in Phainon's message.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Aglaea— Wait, where's Tribbie?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: She began making the necessary preparations the moment we got your message.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The city's citizens are enjoying themselves like it's any other day... Do you not see this as a crisis?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Okhema would be in constant turmoil if we were to raise the alert each time danger befell us. Silently eliminating threats and sparing them from living under the shadow of fear — that is the duty of the Chrysos Heirs.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I don't see things that way... but now's not the time for arguments.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Kafka turns to look at you, her face showing that familiar smile — half cold, half warm.
The Blade of Fury has its aim trained on {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s heart. We need to stop the mad Titan, or the entirety of the holy city could be reduced to ash.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I need an explanation...
Why did I forget about you?

But {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} has crafted an indestructible body for themself, one that can't be entirely destroyed. Mydei is buying us time... We need to cherish every second he's fought for.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You're willing yourself to stay calm, Phainon. That's commendable progress.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Castrum Kremnos has been shrouded in the fog far too long, leaving us unable to discover the mystery behind {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s undying body.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...We can only hope to learn the truth from one Titan.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You mean...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Kafka...
Kafka?
Nonexistent memories begin to cool, frost... then freeze.
Kafka turns away, ignoring your call.
Blade's glance brushes over your face, leaving a burning trail. In your limited encounters with him, you've never seen such... a calm and logical look in his eyes.

Lord Phainon, I will join you in the audience with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}. Let's hope they can restore the visions of the past and reveal the truth behind {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s defiance of death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Why am I with you guys?
I need an explanation...
You have no clue either, Miss Castorice?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Strife and Death used to be inseparable. {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} valued honor in their glory days, so they would never have betrayed their allies back then.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But their pact was broken when {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} descended into madness. From what we know so far... in the pursuit of an immortal body, {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} betrayed Death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: There's one other thing. We found a slate in Kremnos that mentioned an infiltration...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry about that. Tribbie and I will do our best to protect the people of our holy city.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Nonexistent memories begin to cool, frost... then freeze.
Blade turns away, ignoring your call.
Silver Wolf looks up at you, her eyes filled with impatience. You've never spoken with her outside of a hologram — meeting this genius hacker face-to-face is quite novel.
Focus on getting to {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} and using whatever means possible to learn the mad Titan's secrets.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Tribbie is waiting for you outside the city — go with her to the Abyss. I will pray to {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} that you will find success.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Tribbie! We're ready to set off.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Okay, we've been updated on what has happened. Let us send you into the Abyss this time.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Are you sure? It's always been Trianne doing this...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The two trips to and from Castrum Kremnos have completely drained Trianne. She'll need some time to recover.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We can handle this, Snowy... This is as much for De as it is for everyone else.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Nonexistent memories begin to cool, frost... then freeze.
Silver Wolf looks down, ignoring your call.
Firefly turns to you, her expression slightly different from the girl you remember — more melancholic, more profound.
High Priest Tribbie... Do you have any suggestions on how we can get {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} to respond to us later?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sorry... We wish we could help, Cas, but {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} has never been a Titan to chat or interact with humans.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: I suppose... we'll have to rely on ourselves, then.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's one thing to use their powers and another to be aligned with us in war. If that Titan refuses to be on our side... we'll have to resort to a fight.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If that Titan refuses to be on our side... we'll have to resort to a fight.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}... isn't an evil Titan at heart. Let us hope things won't reach that point.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Time is of the essence, everyone... We should get going.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Nonexistent memories begin to cool, frost... then freeze.
Firefly turns away, ignoring your call.
There is very little time left to stay in this memory... Do you want to leave the chance of bidding goodbye to Firefly?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Bid Firefly goodbye.
Need time to think about it.
There is very little time left to stay in this memory... Do you want to leave the chance of bidding goodbye to Kafka?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Bid Kafka goodbye.
This is it! The Century Gate can only take you this far.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Although the Temple of the Three Fates has been abandoned for a long time, the magical barriers woven by the priests still linger around it. Approaching with {RUBY_B#Passage Titan}Janus{RUBY_E#}'s power recklessly could be extremely risky.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We understand. Thank you, Tribbie.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: We have to go back to Okhema to help Aglaea. Snowy and Cas, we trust that you know how to summon us when you're done.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Here, keep this with you. This token is proof of a Janus priest. Hold it up to the Gate of Infinity, and you'll be able to walk through unimpeded.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Take care, alright? May {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} light your path forward.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: We're on our own now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's fantastic.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's fantastic.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Important decisions will be waiting for us every step of the way. What we're about to do will not only determine Mydei's fate... but also that of every single resident in Okhema.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Temple of the Three Fates is behind the Gate of Infinity, and {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} is at the very heart of this temple. We're going to have to find {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} and convince them to help us in our battle.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: May everything go well for us...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This is the path we took when we first arrived.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It is... The world seems to have plummeted to its end in the blink of an eye.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are these... the ruins we saw when we first arrived? They look... somewhat different.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That means you'll come back to me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: That means you'll come back to me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: *incomprehensible speech*
What was that?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I believe that was a Titan speaking... I believe it was {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have to listen closely to what they are saying...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "Devious and repulsive humans... Are you here to disturb my peace again, just as disaster approaches?"
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Name? Mine? Don't remember.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Miss Castorice can understand the Titans' words. That's exactly why we need her on this trip.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Cease your efforts... and let yourself be swallowed by the confusion of time and space..."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Name? Mine? Don't remember.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} is turning us away? It seems like we've hit an obstacle on the very first step.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Could the Titan have created this chaotic scene we see in these ruins as a barrier to hinder us?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We'll overcome any obstacle, no matter what they throw at us.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Tribbie gave us a demonstration when we had to pass through here the last time... It's up to us to recreate these miracles now.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Curse you mortals... curse your pride and your merciless ways."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "Lift the curtain of memory..."
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "...and once again stir the ripples of past reverie!"
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} is saying something again...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "...Who are you to command me? Does your inhumanity know no end?"
rows.speaker: Castorice
