rows.text: This is a lot more destructive than I expected...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Was this giant hand really used for thievery in the past?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Got a crick in your back?
{RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#}, the embodiment of all things despicable.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: No can do, I'm already itching to fight!
Their legacy reduced to mere playthings for humans...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The way ahead is now clear.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus, before we move on... there is something we must explain to you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Hm. You're not here for this foolish competition.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: How did you...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You've been fighting to suppress your true thoughts within you all this while... You cannot deceive me.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I know you have no care for that fatuous king's contrived glory. You can keep your motive to yourselves, so long as you stay out of my way...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I've said it before: To obliterate the deeply entrenched roots of foolishness within Castrum Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Now the true challenge begins... This is where it gets difficult.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Meaningless forestalling. They are meant to taste defeat on the battlefield. Deter us further... and I shall send them to {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Hmph, these goons are much tougher than they seem...
Wahaha, it's my lucky day...
What a fine weapon! It's a real beauty...
With a bit of sprucing up, no one will guess it's second-hand, heh...
...Wait.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: *cough* *cough*
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Got a crick in your back?
No can do, I'm already itching to fight!
*cough* *cough*
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please keep it together, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I wish I could go and help them...
Hush... Listen.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We have our own battle to face.
Heh heheh...
At least we know they're still alive.
Looks like I've hit the jackpot this time...
I hear it now. That's...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Anyone home?
Pretend you did not hear anything. Act oblivious.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Heellooo!
Is he hard of hearing?
What a cranky guy...
We'll find a way to make him come out of hiding.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: What fate?
Stop at the next turn.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Mydeimos... is a deserter?
If there's an assassin... we'll take care of him right there.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Those people sound furious.
...That's why all of your weapons reek of blood.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's the same mechanism... We need to ignite the two braziers to unlock the way forward.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What's wrong with that weapon?
Let's clear this trial together, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What was that just now?
Do you have a plan in mind?
The platform on the right is missing an iron ball...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Talk is cheap. Let's charge in!
Do we have to summon a miracle for it to appear?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's about time you used your powers.
An exquisite stone... It's a shame it appeared somewhere it doesn't belong.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: This competition sounds pretty brutal...
We may be able to temporarily remove it with the orb?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is this competition really that hardcore?
Sign me up!
The bridge ahead is broken. How do we get across?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We'll be his teammates!
The stakes are high...
Let's try illuminating it with the Oronyx Orb.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm not sure about this...
[Trailblazer].
Castorice.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I am the Galactic Baseballer!
Castorice.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Are there others who made it this far...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Observing formalities before aggression, now that's a thoughtful approach.
Never underestimate those who step into this arena. They are skilled and courageous beyond measure.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Do these battle-hardened people also have a taste for puzzles?
So, what is your motive?
Brave one... Step forth...
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Gah!
You could well be... Castrum Kremnos' salvation...
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Huh?
It's you!
Blazing star...
Is that statue... beckoning to us?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Is that Mydei?
What about the festival?
I think... you're right.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Will we have to battle them...?
The aging and feeble king is plotting something unspeakable... One that seeks to defile {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divinity, their soul, and the legacy they left to Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: We need salvation... we need a champion to reignite our hope.
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Why are they doing this?
...I did not come to save anybody, old lion. I am here to answer a call... to crush greed and foolishness once and for all.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: So Nikador is at their mercy?
Perhaps... that's what we desperately need.
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Forge on then, warrior... heed the call. I am elderly... and weary... but I shall watch you depart and pray for victory in every battle encounter...
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Is this one taking more out of you?
Lord Gnaeus, the calling you're heeding...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you need a break, Castorice?
Looks like it wasn't Nikador's idea...
I knew it.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Whoever hatched that plan must've long since turned to ash.
Yikes, our cover's blown...!
Comes from the depths of this city. We're close... so close, in fact, that I can hear the whispers in my ears.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Looks like we'll have to silence him for good!
Castorice...
Such carnage... whose desires does this festival truly serve?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Why don't you take a break...?
What do you mean?
A beast that has lost sight of its target and is now guided only by its innate bloodlust.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: An experiment?
How are you so sure about it?
Lord Gnaeus, now that we're at the very heart of Castrum Kremnos... it's time to let you in on our goal here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We can tap into the power of time again.
While we do not expect you to work with us, we do not wish for conflict either.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ready to travel through time, gladiator?
I can barely believe it myself.
...Speak.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Kremnos must have been through a lot since then...

We came here to find a way to destroy {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}. We received... intel that the Titan of Strife had lost their reason and is now trying to create an immortal vessel for themself.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If we do not stop them now, they will pose a grave danger to the future generations of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: From a time dimension very close to ours...
Hmph, grave danger, you say...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...My companions fighting against Nikador.
Let's just start with these first.
Our goals are not in conflict, girl. Find the Titan and we can both get what we came for.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Better off forgotten.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I smell fear... You're scared?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The souls of the sacrificed are still wandering this hall... I hear their endless bemoaning, their senseless deaths have left them wronged, their mournful wails echo endlessly.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Perhaps I can learn something from their cries...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Reveal yourself, O warrior spirit... I know that you have yet to rest.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I ask for you to guide us. Let us see what you once gazed upon, let us hear what your ears once heard...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You can rouse the dead?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: No... I can only summon souls that haven't fully passed on.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What's wrong, girl?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Guiding souls takes a lot of energy... but I'm fine, Lord Gnaeus.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Out of cowardice. They are afraid of losing their faith and guidance.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: They are fighting against the unseen, they have no time for the folly of mortals.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus, you seem to know a lot about that Titan.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The next one... I need to last till... the next one.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I... I'm fine, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]. There's no need to worry.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Calm yourself, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]... I believe he has no ill intent toward us.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Don't push yourself.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We're almost at the end... I can sense it...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then I'll be the protagonist's bestest sidekick, heehee! So give me more screen time, alright?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I'm fine... {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then I'll be the protagonist's bestest sidekick, heehee! So give me more screen time, alright?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I am sorry... that you had to witness my earlier outburst.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hmph, really now? I wouldn't do something like that!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Says who! I'm still a... a cute and tiny animal, alright!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Forget it. You can skip the translation. I can somehow tell that none of that chatter's meaningful.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The constellation of the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#} is already illuminated. That must mean...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Kremnoans revere strength and military might, but that does not mean we lack etiquette.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You are asking for a reward? Not a problem.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Mydei, what do you mean when you said you were "worried"?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I understand your pain, child. But you need to set it aside for now.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We are nearing the place where they cast and cut the souls.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Where should we start searching?
What a magnificent sight.
It is likely no one survived this far in the festival. Stay alert.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The Titan's kin... Be careful.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But we can just ask around!
Warrior...
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: Ooh, so this is what it feels like to be a time traveler?
Entry... forbidden...
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: Has it lost its sanity? What a woeful creation. I shall put it out of its misery.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Are all these... versions of you from the past?
...Is it dealt with?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You're... a part of Nikador?
What can we do then?
No... I doubt it'll be that simple.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: How do we stop them then?
An experiment...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: King Eurypon wanted to strip {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} of their divinity and seal it within an intricate vessel for all eternity.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We can't put this off any longer.
{F#She}{M#He} knows what it truly means to go to battle. Perhaps {F#she}{M#he} can be your inspiration.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I will do as you wish.
If this is meant to be... then I will fight you.
That's how he would immortalize {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divine body... Of course, he had to test it out on a Titankin before going on to remold the Titan.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The answer's very simple...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...Because the fragments of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s soul are sealed in these statues. The calls that I've been hearing... are coming from them.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: As long as we reassemble their soul and unite their divine core, they will recover their dignity as a Titan. You will then have a chance to triumph over them in battle.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: We've finally found the root of everything...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Castorice carefully takes the weapon in her hand and examines it closely for a moment...
I'll find a way to stall it. To Titankin that have lost all reason, death is as intoxicating as nectar is to bees.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please, you must find a way to make {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s soul whole again. It is only by fixing this point in history... that we can salvage the future of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's see what you can do, delver of memories.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Stay here, warrior... Do not leave your Goddess of Death. The enticing scent of blood here is meant for you, and only you...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sweet... death.
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: Inner... peace.
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: ...Unbelievable.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: This dark and derelict place... is this the future of Kremnos?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The resonance between you and {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} must be strong.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: History has taken a wrong turn... and must be set on the right course once more.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Much time has passed, yet the Titan's soul remains fragmented. That covetous king and his servants would have turned to dust by now... Their scheme that once unfolded here has likewise been buried with them.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: You and I are both here to bring an end to this absurdity. So, join me comrade. Let us bring death unto that Titan.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The sounds of battle. That's...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...Let me through.
rows.speaker: Silent Gladiator

rows.text: Why, it's you again, inarticulate fool! Pfft, unarmed, and yet you dare to think you can join the Kremnos Festival? That's an insult to the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#}!
rows.speaker: Kremnos Registration Officer

rows.text: I've told you before — this is a trial for three! This is a trial that requires three people! If you can't even gather enough comrades to stand by you in life and death, it's time you went home and took up herding!
rows.speaker: Kremnos Registration Officer

rows.text: ...Let me through.
rows.speaker: Silent Gladiator

rows.text: So, there are mortals who fight against fate even in this hopelessly bleak era. I am impressed.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: But strength alone will not help them destroy an immortal body... That's why you and that girl went back in time seeking answers.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "Courage."
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "Honor."
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "Tenacity."
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "Sacrifice."
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "Reason."
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: There are only four soul-forged statues here. If they did split {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divinity into five parts, there is still one fragment of the soul that is missing.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Agreed.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: There's no trace... Let's just start with these first.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Come, help me piece together Strife's divinity.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...Gnaeus.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I can hear... I hear it.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...Gnaeus.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: A part of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divinity is sealed within this...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "We shall hereby seal the god-king's Courage within this sword vessel."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: May your courageous souls satisfy {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} and fuel the conquests of Kremnos.
rows.speaker: Kremnos Registration Officer

rows.text: "A testament that they have never once retreated from a battle."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "Even against the formless black tide from beyond the dense fog, they alone have raised their sword and faced the enemy head-on..."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Courage...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The voices... are starting to pour in.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Here lies another fragment of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divinity...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "We shall hereby seal the god-king's Honor within this sword vessel."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "A testament that they have never plunged their divine lance into an enemy's back."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "Even when enemies close in from all sides, they have never conceded to evil schemes, fiercely guarding the warrior's dignity..."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: Brave one... O Brave one! Come closer... Let me get a good look at you...
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: Are you calling out to me, lion?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: That's right... I am. You have an unusual aura about you... I have not seen such a blazing soul in a very long time.
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: The blazing star of Castrum Kremnos has drifted far from us... all that remains is a dim candle, on the verge of being extinguished.
rows.speaker: Chryseus Leo

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Honor...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I am listening...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Go on... Tell me your tale.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "We shall hereby seal the god-king's Tenacity within this sword vessel."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "A testament that their will is unyielding in the fight against the calamity of unknown origin."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "No matter how powerful the black tide may be, enough to corrupt the wills of other gods, they stand tall and upright in defiance of the turbulent fog, even till today..."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Tenacity...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Divinity exists within this statue.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Tell me everything that happened here...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: "We shall hereby seal the god-king's Sacrifice within this sword vessel."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "A testament that their final words before sinking into dormancy were a vow to defend the world against the black tide."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: "They use their own body as our city walls, keeping out and protecting us from the pervasive spread of madness. They are acutely aware that if the end times were to arrive, there would be nothing left in this world to conquer..."
rows.speaker: Festival Noise

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Sacrifice...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Hm... We're now left with the final missing fragment of divinity.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: I was wrong all this while. The final fragment of divinity was never lost...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus, are we almost there?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes... There is just one last thing to do.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: No one knows when the black tide first appeared beyond the distant horizon, but when it slowly encroached upon Amphoreus' borders, {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} was the first Titan to venture forth.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: During the battle against the black tide, their sanity began to slip away... In their prime, the Titan could obliterate an entire archipelago with a single slash, yet they could not sever the root of this corruption.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Split... soul...
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: Indestructible... body...!
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: They battled the black tide by sheer will alone, but ultimately succumbed to it. Before their divinity could be completely corrupted, they removed a part of it...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Could it be...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Split... soul...
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: The fragment of divinity that they stripped away — the fragment they wanted to preserve the most — was Reason.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The Titan believed that their Reason would someday respond to their calling, to return to their body... and fulfill their sacred mission.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: All of these... They're—
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: They represent countless failed endeavors. With your help, I can finally put an end to everything.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Indestructible... body...
rows.speaker: Furiae Praetor

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus... What do you intend to do?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Courage, Honor, Tenacity, and Sacrifice... they're all versions of me. Hearing the murmurs of these soul fragments has led me to a conclusion.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador's{RUBY_E#} soul is corrupted beyond the point of salvation.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: There is only one option.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: There is only one way to do so.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The seal that binds their divinity is already broken. As long as we complete the soul-forging here, {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} will be whole once more.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: You will go into battle with a Titan nearly at the zenith of their powers. And when that happens, the glory of slaying a god will also be presented before you.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...What about you, Lord Gnaeus?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I will return to where I came from and become a part of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s divinity once more.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: In all likelihood, I will also be consumed by corruption. An inevitable course of action if we hope to end this madness.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: You are willing to... sacrifice yourself for a future you won't get to witness?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This is my purpose, my origin. I am no mortal and I do not fear death... Even so, will you still weep for me?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: All farewells in this world are sorrowful, Lord Gnaeus.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: While we haven't known each other for long, I have learned much from you. In return, I'll teach you a lesson of mine before I go...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Do not detest your talent and do not abhor death. Journeys and epics are only glorious and magnificent because all things eventually fade to dust.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: ...The embodiment of Strife telling me about the majesty of the world...? What an irony...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Civilizations only grow under strife. Humans instinctively loathe suffering, yet suffering is the only thing that teaches them to stand unyielding and tall...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: If you die by my lance, then there's no need to reflect on what I said. But if you should send me to my grave... promise me that you will use my Coreflame to fuel a roaring blaze and continue the fight against the black tide.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: On behalf of all the Chrysos Heirs, I... promise you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I am {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, the Lance of Fury, the messenger of turmoil, and the embodiment of Strife!
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Remember this: I am the scar that this world needs!
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: It's finally over.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Lord {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, can you hear me?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I know that your only wish right now is to rest in peace. But you are the only one with answers to my deepest doubts... So, forgive me for disturbing you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please, tell me... do you know where {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} is?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I must find them. The half of me that I've been deprived of since birth... I must take it back from them.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (Titan's fragmented voice)
rows.speaker: Nikador's Corpse

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Time passes quickly. It's been a long time since the last Titan fell...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (Titan's fragmented voice)
rows.speaker: Nikador's Corpse

rows.text: Now that the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#} is no more, we Chrysos Heirs are one step closer to the genesis as foretold in the prophecy.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The silence here is stifling... This city feels so unfamiliar now that its Titan is gone.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: You've exchanged thousands of blows with them... Your ears are probably just not used to this peace and quiet.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Hmph. What's next?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Some time later...
I have an agreement with the Titan... The Chrysos Heirs will take away their Coreflame and use it to start a bright blaze that'll illuminate our path onward.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You... spoke with {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What did they say? Please, I need to know...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Something out there? Please, I need to know what it is...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Not now, Lord Mydei. I'll tell you everything once we return to Okhema.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Aglaea mentioned that... someone must touch the Coreflame and absorb it to become its temporary receptacle.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Mydei, do you...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...This honor is yours. Isn't it something you've been longing for?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: But you're more deserving of it... You sustained all these new wounds from fighting them.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If you have any idea how exhausting it is to fight a protracted battle...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Then you should know that pointless arguments are the last thing I want to get into now.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Meh, a little back and forth wouldn't hurt much. Coming to a decision so easily makes it seem like this is not at all a life-changing undertaking, you know.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Come with me then, Coreflame. The Vortex of Genesis is awaiting your return.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Are you alright, Phainon?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I don't think I felt anything at all.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Or rather... it felt a lot easier than I expected? I had assumed that bearing the Coreflame would take... a lot more out of me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In any case, let's return to Okhema and share news of our victory with the two demigods.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Leave, friend? Return, together?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Although he was but a part of {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}... he was nevertheless a hero in his own right.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Go with the rest, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]. I will catch up with you later. I would like to talk to Lord Gnaeus again... one last time.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I see... So even the Strife Titan has never seen Death in the flesh.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I will continue this arduous journey, even if I must travel to every corner of Amphoreus...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I understand... The Chrysos Heirs will fulfill the promise we made and see your unfinished work to its end.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Such a peaceful end is not befitting of you, the bringer of Strife into this world... But it's a good thing it's just me here. No one else can see what you look like in the final moments of your life.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Poets will still describe you as an embodiment of madness and corruption, the god of war who incinerated all of their glory. Yet, at this moment... I am willing to send you into the gentle embrace of death, to a sweet land full of blossoming flowers.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Farewell, Titan.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Agy, they're back!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: You and Dan Heng watch Phainon leave the bath...
We completed the mission, Tribbie! No broken limbs or severe injuries, just a fiery Coreflame in the palm of my hand.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I can feel the Coreflame's warmth... Well done, Phainon.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It has been far too long since Amphoreus last saw the birth of a demigod. Having you take {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}'s place will surely invigorate the spirits of those in the holy city.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Exhaustion envelops you... At this moment, no god of Amphoreus could pull your gaze away from this lounge chair.

I... want to be honest about this: I believe Mydei is the better candidate. He was once the crown prince of Kremnos after all, and much of his lifetime was spent fighting alongside {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: He is more worthy of the title of "Strife" than I am.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Wait... Something seems off...
...Did you notice?
You have thought much about this, sweet child, but there is one thing you overlooked.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The qualities you've mentioned are very likely the reasons Mydeimos refused this Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I do not doubt his strength and talents... In fact, he must have imagined himself becoming a god a thousand times over. But he turned it down because he does not want to lead his people down the same path again.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: So I will ask you once more... Have you made up your mind, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I am ready for this. I will shoulder the burden of divinity alongside the both of you... I am willing to make the necessary sacrifices.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Very good.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: This day has finally come, Snowy. You've been wanting this all along, right?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Your consciousness sinks into dreams, and at the edge of the dreamscape, you hear a whisper...
While you were having the strange dream, somewhere else in Okhema...
If the prophecy hadn't found me back then... I would still be roaming the world aimlessly. Right now though, I live for the sole purpose of dedicating myself to the mission of the Chrysos Heirs.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I never once doubted your resolve.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: This time tomorrow, the Chrysos Heirs will gather at the Vortex of Genesis to surrender the Coreflame that once belonged to {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, the Lance of Fury.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Remember, this is unlike the unchanging rites our priests perform. No one knows the true cost a mortal must pay to accept Strife's divine authority. Your road ahead is still full of uncertainty.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Use this time to properly rest, Phainon.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I understand. Until tomorrow, then.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It's so peaceful, as if nothing even happened.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The people of Amphoreus must have extraordinary spirits to be able to enjoy their lives even in such troubled times.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...They have Aglaea and Tribbie to thank for that. It is because of their protection that the citizens are able to enjoy peace.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Where did Mydei go?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: He was exhausted, so he already went back to rest.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Our victory might not have been possible without your help. I'm sure you've heard enough words of gratitude, but it's only right that I—
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Right, it would be the first time I thanked you. So, thank you for your help, uh... Miss Mem?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Aglaea will gather us at the Vortex of Genesis this time tomorrow, where we'll perform a ritual to surrender the Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: She only mentioned the Chrysos Heirs, but if I invite you two... I'm sure she'll welcome your presence.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Is there anything we should know about this ritual?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: From what Aglaea said, no one can predict what's going to happen, because each Titan's divine authority is unique. That's why I hope both of you can be there tomorrow. It'll bolster my confidence.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hahaha, that's settled then.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Uh, that can be on Aglaea's tab. She's also known as the Goldweaver. Doesn't that name alone sound wealthy?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hahaha, I'll be sure to send someone to wake you up then.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The night's all yours, but get some rest before tomorrow's ritual. I should also take this time to sort out my thoughts... I'll see you soon, my friends.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Did you pick up on that, [Trailblazer]? He seems troubled.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You should start observing people's body language and their microexpressions. You can learn a lot from them.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: From his body language and... microexpressions.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I guess it's understandable, seeing how he's about to experience something extraordinary. The Titans may only be local gods of Amphoreus, but a mortal ascending to something else altogether... sounds like a lot to take in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...You're right. So much happened in so short a time that we haven't had the time to consider our own predicament.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Our car's scrap, we've lost contact with the Crew, and everything beyond the sky is taboo here...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's a pity we can't send March a message, so she can help you finish your dailies.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I do have some old-timey games with me, but I doubt you'd be interested.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Once Phainon's ascension ritual is over, we should start working out these problems of ours.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: For now though, let's just head back to the bath chamber to rest and gather ourselves.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Aww, are you sleepy? I can see your eyelids growing heavy~
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Go to sleep then, if you're tired. Snoozy snooze... But isn't it always daytime in this city? How do you fall asleep like this...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Eep! I'll get embarrassed if you keep staring at me like that.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Are there... knots in my fur? Is it my ears? No, they seem fine. Look, I can even flap them!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Hmm? You're right! I am speaking in full sentences now!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Wowie! It feels amazing being able to speak fluently! But... why do I speak in such a proper, un-cutesy manner now? I mean, referring to myself in standard first person and all.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Personality...? Hmph, you're always saying things I don't understand!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Right!? You noticed too? Hmph, no fair!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I didn't ask to be like this! No judging!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hmph, never mind, since I'm the forgiving type. Besides, now that I'm a bit more used to it... I don't sound as bad?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Huh... I don't remember a thing about myself. Ugh, my head hurts.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I have a gut feeling, though! As long as we continue to collect the fragments of memories scattered across Amphoreus, we'll be rewarded with something really, really good.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: How should I put it... Bah, anyway! I just know that this world is very important to me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I'm not a dog! Or a pet! I am...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Uh, what am I? A—Anyhow, I'm an important character for sure!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hnngh... I think I'm getting sleepy. The light feels so nice and warm. Even my fur's toasty warm. I can fall asleep any...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Zzz... Zzz...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You should take this opportunity to rest, Lord Phainon... The Coreflame ritual is tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Today, tomorrow, what difference does it make? It's always morning in Okhema under {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s protection.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So long as the light continues to shine this brightly, I won't be getting any sleep. Why force myself to shut my eyes when I can instead take this time to calm my mind and gather my thoughts? That counts as rest too.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Have you... thought things through then?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Not at all. Everything's a jumbled mess still. I don't even know where to start.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Coreflame was blazing hot in my palm in the beginning, but it has completely cooled off now... I can barely feel it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Miss Castorice... Does this mean I'm a good match for {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I don't quite get how it works, but if it's going to put you at ease... then I will say yes to that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's the Abyss in the distance... Oh, that reminds me of the question I didn't get to ask.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Back in the temple with the Scales of Justice, when {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} was trying to deter us... Why did you stop me, Miss Castorice?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Because I knew there must be another solution. "Something more important than the fate of Amphoreus"... It is far too cruel and unfair to ask that of you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You should know that I would've gone ahead if Dan Heng hadn't come up with an answer in time.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I know. We should not have hesitated then. I stopped you before I even realized it myself...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...It's fortunate we had the both of them there with us.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yeah, it's a good thing we had them.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Are you still thinking about the past, Lord Phainon?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Every waking moment.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I lied to the two demigods just now. I told them the duty of the Chrysos Heirs is all I think about now. Do you think I managed to slip by Aglaea's golden threads this time?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No one fools her, Lord Phainon. She merely chooses to turn a blind eye to our lies.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You're right. How foolish of me to think I got away with it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I often wonder if someone as ordinary as me can really become a hero. I thought defeating {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} would quell the voice of doubt in my mind... but it has only grown louder.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I don't have the right words for you now, but... I know you're far from ordinary, Lord Phainon. Mydei often calls you "Deliverer" in jest, but I don't believe he means it mockingly.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I should probably shut out these pointless thoughts and empty my mind until the hour of the ritual...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I did that before sitting for Tribbie's history exam — who in the world could hope to go over those piles of documents and slates? I decided I was better off resigning myself to fate. That way I'd get more time to play and practice with my sword.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...How did you do on the exam then?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: My score? I don't remember anymore. All I remember is Tribbie punishing me to a full week of cleaning the Chrysos Heirs' bath. And no one was allowed to help me.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So High Priest Tribbie can be strict too...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please continue with this mentality, Lord Phainon. I believe you'll be alright.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Thank you, Miss Castorice. I think I'll stay here for a little while and keep all of those unruly thoughts out. It's not like anything will come of them, anyway.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The sights of Aedes Elysiae — my homeland — have been flashing before my eyes lately.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Those Kremnoans mastered some cutting-edge technology... If only I could separate my soul from my body too. That way, I'd be able to fly my soul back to the comforting fields of my homeland any time.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's the only place I can be momentarily at peace...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Ah, an utterly ■■■ adventure! Feel free to replace ■■■ with whatever description you see fit!
I bet you're as curious as I am. So! What's going to happen next?
Heh, keep it together. All that excitement isn't going to get you anywhere, you know. Why don't you follow me into another tale on the other side of the cosmos...?
Ta-da! Recognize this place? Herta Space Station — the base of a genius and the cradle of science.
Look at these puppets! Aren't they dearly exquisite? Let's just say I've already heard many others secretly gushing, "She looks so pretty" on more than one occasion...
If you ask me though, they barely did justice to Madam Herta's beauty! Maybe just 10%... no, not even 1% of the real deal! Now I'm no fawner here, just stating an objective fact...

Remember this scene? Gah, it evoked so much emotion in me! The esteemed Madam Herta, Genius Society #83, asking the great Nous a question! An attempt to gain a peek into the divinities' mysteries through THEM!
Alright, so continuing from where we left off last time, this is where everything would begin for the genius smart enough to rewrite the history of the entire cos—
...Tsk, Fourth Mirror. Who exactly are you talking to?
rows.speaker: Noble Female Voice

rows.text: Wh—Why, I was just ramping it up for our grand appearance, Madam Herta.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Hm. So, a dramatic debut...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...But what are the odds of that happening!? Sure, slightly plausible if I did manage to talk to Droidhead, but guess what's the problem...? THEY have no reaction whatsoever!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Err... But look at this, Madam Herta... You're standing before Nous here! Right there.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Oh, that? That's a hologram. What? I can't possibly summon the real Droidhead here, can I?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...You mean to say you've just been reciting your lines before a hologram!?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: What's this, ma'am?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Mm, looks like one of those Memory Bubbles. It's not worth that much attention. You'll find many more in the other zones.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hmm... is that so.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: There's a Memory Bubble here too...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Why are you so interested in it?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Okay, I'll admit it. I find them somewhat... creepy?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: A Memory Bubble tucked away this far in?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Heh... I think I know what this is about now. This is interesting.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But we can leave that for later... Let's take care of the malfunctioning puppets first.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Madam Herta... We picked up some voices from the space.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Hmm? Let me hear them.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Is this... binary arithmetic? Could it be Droidhead?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait, there shouldn't be a "2" in binary arithmetic!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Is this some kind of prank...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Madam Herta! We're hearing those voices again!
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: What now? What should we do!?
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: Keep your cool, Second Mirror. What did they say this time? Play it again for me.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait a minute. This door... isn't locked?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: Door...? Locked...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No, this isn't the Voice of the Path at all...! What in the world is going on?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hyuk hyuk hyuk... Madam Herta, those lads outside... seem to be discussing something interesting...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Wanna listen in on them? Hyuk hyuk hyuk...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Third Mirror! Stop that nightmarish cackle. It's giving me goosebumps.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait, did you say "those lads outside"? Could it be...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Eheheh... Why don't you listen for yourself?
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: She fainted?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: Mm-hmm, looks like it.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: ...This isn't right. I'm sure we've got intruders in the lab!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Should we rouse her, Mr. Yang?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: ...Let's do it. I'm not sure she'll be happy about it, but we have no time to waste.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: ...Wait! S—Stop whatever you're about to do...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No, don't even think about it! Whoever you are, you'd better not interrupt me right now!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I must continue forward... Just a few more steps and I'll be able to see Droidhead!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: (Now that I think about it, I don't think March has ever fallen sick before.)
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (What is different about this time, though...?)
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Pom-Pom, have you prepared our meals already?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course, the food's ready! March isn't feeling well, so Pom-Pom has specially prepared the conductor's special bland meal that'll be easy on her stomach.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Can you bring it to her, Himeko?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Gladly. Why don't we also get her a—
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Nuh-uh! No coffee when she's already feeling unwell!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Heh... I guess you're right.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Outside Amphoreus, in a familiar corner of the Cosmos...
Yeah, creating dramatic value. Isn't that what you're most obsessed with?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Moving on. Don't try, but you wouldn't even begin to imagine how difficult it is to send a message to Nous. And I went all out for it...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Powering the Audience System alone required me to reconfigure the energy supply of the entire space station! I had to switch it to Hibernate mode before rebooting everything. Do you have any idea how much that costs?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...How much? How much?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Uh...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...I'm not in charge of finance. Go pose that to Asta instead.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: So you don't know either!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: I am Herta herself, the Emanator of Erudition and a true-blue genius. Why would I be holding the purse strings? That menial task is beneath me.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You're absolutely right, Madam Herta! The IPC should really be providing a genius like you with all that you require, so you can freely dive into any research that tickles your fancy!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: With that said, Herta herself, Emanator of Erudition, and true-blue genius... What do you plan to do now?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: What else can I do? Identify what's malfunctioning within the Audience System and fix it, of course.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Um... Don't take offense to my candid words, Madam Herta. You may be proficient in many aspects, but... is hands-on work really one of your strong suits?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Um... I humbly suggest for you to contact Stephen instead...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Contact him and expose how I shelled out a bomb to send a message to Droidhead, only to screw up everything else?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Mm, alright, alright. I get it...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Good that you do.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: There. That's the Audience System's terminal. Come, walk with me. We'll check what's wrong with it.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Aye-aye, ma'am! Oh, but I can't walk. I can only float...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: What's with your witty remarks today?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hmm... This is the Audience System? It looks just like the Simulated Universe.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Keen observation. They share the same fundamental logic, and are pretty much identical in that regard.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ahh, I see. We call this... referencing, and not appropriation, right? Heh...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: One more stupid remark from you and you can watch Fifth Mirror reference your role, because I'm going to be dropping you as my assistant.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Focus now. The Audience System is divided into three zones: Energy Supply, Computing, and Communications. Each zone operates independently, and will only be integrated via the Path of Erudition when the system is booted.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Sending a message to Droidhead involves more intricacies than you can imagine. If routine trials and maintenance on such an elaborately sophisticated system are already as bad as squaring circles, then it's no surprise for glitches like this to crop up.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I see. So, Madam Herta, can you use your professional judgment to tell which zone the glitch is in?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Of course. All three.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No sweat. They'll be up and running again after some simple technical tweaking.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The three zones are compartmentalized, so we're going to have to troubleshoot them one at a time. Let's start with the Energy Supply Zone. Get ready, and then we'll go over.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I'm just a mirror, Madam Herta! If you're ready, then your reflection in me will also be ready to go.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Brr... Why is this Energy Supply Zone... so cold? Brr... I—I'm already frosting up!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Hmph, why else? I've converted the energy core that supplies all of Herta Space Station into Imaginary state and stored it in this zone. If not for the ultra-low temperature here, the space station would have long blasted off into the sky.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Brrr... But... aren't we already... in the sky?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: ...You're just a mirror. I don't need you to take on comic relief too.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Where did those things come from? Corrupted data? Reanimated systemic rust? No, not likely... It can't be the Legion's second ambush, right...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Meh, whatever. We have to get rid of them anyway. Alright, stay close and try to avoid shattering to pieces!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Brrr... Aaaaand Madam Herta never fails to impress! Those things are no match for you!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Hmph, a piece of cake!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Now that this place is cleaned up, let's set everything in order and move on to the next zone.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wh—What in the...!? How did all these disgusting bugs get in here?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: We're going to need out-of-this-world computing capability if we hope to meet Droidhead. If we can't churn out calculations faster than a yottaFLOPS computer, then we can forget about having THEM notice our existence.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But computers with too high a computing capability tend to attract Computing Stings like them. No one knows how these creatures evolved from their progenitor — the Propagation.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ah, the mysteries of life. Hah! But even so, they can't compare to a talking mirror~
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: A question on the side, Madam Herta: You have these powerful supercomputers and all, so... um, what are they normally programmed to calculate?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Is that important? All that matters is that they work and are able to attract Droidhead's attention.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: *sigh* ...I suggest meeting Miss Asta for a chat when you have time.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Ew, yuck! Help me! Goo from those bugs got onto my reflective surface!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Clean up after yourself. Can't you just wipe it off with your hands?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Ahaha! Good one there...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: With those annoying bugs squashed, we're done fixing the Computing Zone too.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: These computers will get up to speed soon. Now we're just one final step away from requesting an audience with Droidhead.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Our last stop is the... Communications Zone?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Oh? You have a good memory. Let's go see what's wrong in that zone.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Egads, what a close shave... But why are these Remembrance memes even showing up here?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: That's not the only one. Look at them. #7631 and #10136... are affected too.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Can't you do a factory reset on them?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Sorry to disappoint. The "Absolutely Not Module" has been enabled, so not even I get to bypass its permissions. Whoopsie.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...What were you really trying to achieve with these creations?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Just some toys to amuse myself with.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Finding the source of the corruption can wait. These puppets no longer have use now that I'm here. Take them all out! Defective goods ought to be sent back to the repair center!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I... urge you to go easy on them, for the sake of the space station...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: They're completely battered, save for... their heads?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Never strike someone in the face — the same goes for puppets.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I'm picking up signals from more puppets somewhere farther in. Let's go take a look.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Phew, that was close... I almost shattered...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Don't be melodramatic. Working even a single brain cell of mine to take out foes like her is an outright waste of my smarts.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I take it we've taken care of the problems in all three zones? Does that mean...?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Not yet. There's something else we need to deal with.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What's this, ma'am?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Mm, looks like one of those Memory Bubbles. It's not worth that much attention. You'll find many more in the other zones.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hmm... is that so.
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: There's a Memory Bubble here too...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Why are you so interested in it?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Okay, I'll admit it. I find them somewhat... creepy?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: A Memory Bubble tucked away this far in?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Heh... I think I know what this is about now. This is interesting.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But we can leave that for later... Let's take care of the malfunctioning puppets first.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Madam Herta... We picked up some voices from the space.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Hmm? Let me hear them.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Is this... binary arithmetic? Could it be Droidhead?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait, there shouldn't be a "2" in binary arithmetic!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Is this some kind of prank...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Madam Herta! We're hearing those voices again!
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: What now? What should we do!?
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: Keep your cool, Second Mirror. What did they say this time? Play it again for me.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait a minute. This door... isn't locked?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: Door...? Locked...?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No, this isn't the Voice of the Path at all...! What in the world is going on?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hyuk hyuk hyuk... Madam Herta, those lads outside... seem to be discussing something interesting...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Wanna listen in on them? Hyuk hyuk hyuk...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Third Mirror! Stop that nightmarish cackle. It's giving me goosebumps.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Wait, did you say "those lads outside"? Could it be...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Eheheh... Why don't you listen for yourself?
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: She fainted?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: Mm-hmm, looks like it.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: ...This isn't right. I'm sure we've got intruders in the lab!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Should we rouse her, Mr. Yang?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: ...Let's do it. I'm not sure she'll be happy about it, but we have no time to waste.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: ...Wait! S—Stop whatever you're about to do...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: No, don't even think about it! Whoever you are, you'd better not interrupt me right now!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I must continue forward... Just a few more steps and I'll be able to see Droidhead!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It seems we've had a little tagalong all this while...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You've got quite the sharp eye, Madam Herta. Would you like us to help?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Sure, go ahead and summon the whole team, Fourth Mirror.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Considering the gravity of our endeavor, we can't allow a little thief to spoil the show.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hmph, parasite of the Remembrance. Do you truly think your atrocious disguise can outwit the keen sight of a genius like myself?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Once you're reflected in my mirrors...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...you can forget about escaping.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh dear, oh dear. This is bad...
rows.speaker: Memosnatcher

rows.text: Right, stay alive and again I can strive... Retreat into the Memory Zone for now, I can always regroup and try again!
rows.speaker: Memosnatcher

rows.text: Someone hasn't been paying attention.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Didn't hear me, did you? With those petty tricks of yours... do you actually think you can slip away right under my nose?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Herta... Madam Herta, wait! Wh—What do you want with me...?
rows.speaker: Memosnatcher

rows.text: I... I'll spill it all! The Garden's secrets and what they're after... everything! P—Please just spare me...
rows.speaker: Memosnatcher

rows.text: Well, is that all you've got to say while your life is at stake? That's hardly worth anything.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Need a little refresher? I am Herta, Genius Society #83, the one to unravel the mystery behind the imaginary leakage phenomenon, and keyholder of the Imaginary Implosion Pulse... Do you honestly believe I'd seek any counsel from you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hush now, keep quiet. This is my moment to shine, so just listen.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You crept in here to steal Nous' memories, didn't you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: And messing with my precious Audience System is just a ruse to lure me here so I can lead you to THEM...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What a shame. You're only a step away from completing the mission assigned to you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Mmph...! Nngh...!
rows.speaker: Memosnatcher

rows.text: ...As if. Truth is, you never stood a chance from the get-go, teehee!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Think I only have Fourth Mirror following me around? Then you've let your guard down, because her siblings have long been watching your every move. Now, let me think... What kind of punishment should I subject a brazen thief like you to?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ooh, I know! You Garden folk have a fondness for mirrors, huh... How about letting you enjoy some quality time with your favorite object — a mirror?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: As for the length of your punishment... Let's keep it mildly punitive. How about a hundredth of a lifetime? That should be enough for some serious self-reflection.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Aww, cheer up. You can still do your part for this world while trapped in a mirror. For all you know, your weak Path Energy could just help me get Droidhead looking this way.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ah, I should make myself clear. When I said a hundredth of a lifetime...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...I meant my lifetime.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ahh, at long last... We can finally be at ease now that we've nipped those problems in the bud.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Omnomnom... Mmm, this is yummy...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Cut that out! Those weird noises make me seem like I've got a few screws loose. Put that little thief to sleep for now. We can decide her fate later.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, sweet and venerable Madam Herta, when did your heart turn this tender?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: The Audience System has been rebooted. This is finally it...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: After all that I've done to reach you, Droidhead... You'd better not snub me.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: (The Path Space... This isn't a figment of the Simulated Universe, but a perfectly tangible and accessible space...)
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: (Right. Now's not the time to wallow in nostalgia. Droidhead... Will you answer me?)
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Is something wrong, Madam Herta?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: No, it's nothing. I was just thinking...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Um, Madam Herta... I think you'll want to listen to the voices from beyond this space...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: I'll leave it to you then, Mr. Sunday.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: My pleasure.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: Wait... What are they up to?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Please pardon me, Madam Herta—
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: Is this... the Harmony?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ridiculous! Hoping to stop me with such cheap parlor tricks? Not a chance!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: She easily dispelled the Resonance with her subconscious mind... as expected of an Emanator.
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 2

rows.text: Is there something else we can try?
rows.speaker: Voice of Path 1

rows.text: Bahaha! Presumptuous fellows. Who are you to interrupt Madam Herta's experiment?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Let's ignore them and keep going. We haven't seen Nous yet!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: ...Forget it, mirror. Let's just leave.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Leave? S—Surely you're not suggesting... we stop the Audience Experiment right now?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: That's beyond all reason, ma'am! We went through so much just to get here! Now we're just one step away from making contact with the Aeon THEMSELF... Please, you know how insanely costly it is to reboot the Audience System!
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: But if I were to ignore those two intruders and continue onward... When Droidhead casts THEIR gaze upon the space station, the blast of energy generated in that instant is sure to burn them to a crisp.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Experiments can always be repeated, but humans cannot be brought back to life.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: *sob* Oh Madam Herta, so selfless and kind! I am truly... truly a lucky mirror to have found the best... best possible master...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Enough. Don't use that nauseatingly fawning tone on me!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Looks like I'll have to abort this prematurely again.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But mark my words, Droidhead: I will be back for you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Madam Herta? You're finally awake.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...You two...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: My plan is ruined! And it's all thanks to you!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Your plan?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My sincerest apologies, Madam Herta... We weren't aware this was a part of your plan.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The space station was in complete darkness when we arrived, so Sunday and I assumed something bad had happened. We continued further into the space station, hoping to find the cause of the blackout... and that's when we chanced upon your... actual self.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: How did you get in?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: The door wasn't locked.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Alright, fine... I am a person of reason, after all. You're not to blame for this.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I am familiar with Mr. Yang of the Astral Express, but the one next to you...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Looks like Madam Herta doesn't pay much attention to cosmic news.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Please pardon my manners. It is unbecoming of me to forget the most basic of courtesies amid all that has happened... My name is Sunday, and I'm just a passenger of the Express.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And this unremarkable passenger... happens to be a Harmony Pathstrider? Hmph, do you take me for a child?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: In any case, I don't suppose you came all the way here just to check on how the space station is doing?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Well, we were worried for a moment there... but it's good to know the space station isn't in any kind of trouble.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We're here because of Amphoreus, Madam Herta.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hm. Why does that not surprise me?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh? Something occured to you?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No, I've told Himeko everything I know. Nothing about the world sounds right. Droidhead has cast THEIR gaze upon numerous worlds in the past... and every one of them is etched in my mind. So how could I possibly not know about it?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Perhaps those Garden folks lied to you. Anyhow, I've looked up the name Amphoreus in the Simulated Universe. Though clearly irrelevant results have already been filtered out...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: There's still an unbelievably long list of generated results. Something about how the Divine Amphoreus team will swap out their current crest emblem for one in King Baviru's likeness in the next season. I hope that can be of some help to you.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...We may as well take a look at it.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I still don't get it, though. Didn't the Astral Express already depart some time ago? Is that world so incredibly spectacular that it warrants this return trip?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Well, that's because... we're caught between a rock and a hard place.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If Amphoreus is indeed inextricably entwined with Aeons, Paths, and even the Erudition, we're going to need the wisdom of a genius to help us. Especially now that we've seen the planet for ourselves.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Elaborate a little on this "rock and a hard place" you're caught between?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: We've lost all contact with two indispensable companions since they entered Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: And that's not all... One of our other companions is suffering from a serious and inexplicable affliction.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Good thing you're finally up! Or that Giant's light is going to give you a sunburn!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: They've been this excited for a while now... What did you feed them?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Forget it. You can skip the translation. I can somehow tell that none of that chatter's meaningful.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's almost time. The Chrysos Heirs should be finishing up their preparations at the Vortex of Genesis.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's go witness the Coreflame's return when you're ready.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "O majesty of the twelve Titans, pillars of the world—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "We seek your divinity, to mend the rifts of the world—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "Fill our bodies with blood of gold, till we wither in willing service to the prophecy..."
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Your guests are here, Phainon. We can begin the ritual now.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon steers his own fate.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Lord Mydei isn't here yet...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You have a lot of faith in him.
It's fine, Miss Castorice. He spoke to me already.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What if he fails?
I told him that he should be nursing his wounds, and that he shouldn't be worrying about all this comrade's once-in-a-lifetime ascension ritual stuff.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So, I'm ready to begin.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: There will come a day when he leads everyone — everyone we have left — through the gates of the miracle.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Phainon steers his own fate.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: There will come a day when he leads everyone — everyone we have left — through the gates of the miracle.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Zzz... Zzz...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Teacher, show him the way forward.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Snowy... zzz... will succeed...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Zzz... Zzz...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Snowy... zzz... will succeed...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Despite the myriad dark and endless nights that have gone by, the guidance of the prophecy is nevertheless as clear and bright as the first ray of dawn.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: You seem worried.
Overthrow the gods, it declared.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: You spoke to him?
Restore the Coreflames, it declared.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Bear the divine authority, it declared.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Wherever he is, whatever he is fighting, I pray he makes it through this test.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wherever he is, whatever he is fighting, I pray he makes it through this test.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: A number of thin sheets of ice have shackled the unconscious March 7th to her bed. The once warm bedroom is now permeated with a bitter cold.
The young girl lays silent and flawless in the ice... Just as she did back when she was drifting through space.
Curled up in the clear ice, the young girl remains silent with her eyes fixed shut.
Although the ice is not cold to the touch, there is something particularly saddening about seeing a young girl who is normally so full of life fall into complete silence.
More like they snuck food themself.
Hmph, really now? I wouldn't do something like that!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: They don't seem to need food.
Says who! I'm still a... a cute and tiny animal, alright!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Forge miracles, it declared.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Oops, missed the party...
O prophecy, forgive us for this late tribute. We Chrysos Heirs have striven to start the Flame-Chase Journey anew over these myriad nights. The seeds we sowed have finally yielded a good harvest.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Phainon said you weren't coming.
Isn't it nice to be polite?
Kremnoans revere strength and military might, but that does not mean we lack etiquette.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Talk is cheap.
You are asking for a reward? Not a problem.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The seventh Coreflame needed for the miracle, that once belonged to the great Lance of Fury, {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#}, shall now be returned by an elected hero of the Chrysos Heirs: An upstanding citizen, a valiant warrior, and a noble soul.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: To Be Continued
Hmm...
Please step forward, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Mmm...?
Recite with us:
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "O majesty of the twelve Titans, pillars of the world—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon & Phainon

rows.text: "We seek your divinity, to mend the rifts of the world—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon & Phainon

rows.text: "Fill our bodies with blood of gold, till we wither in willing service to the prophecy..."
rows.speaker: Trinnon & Phainon

rows.text: Surrender the Coreflame, Chrysos Heir.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: What a... mysterious ritual. Is there really nothing we can do but wait?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't know about the rest of them, but I don't like to just sit by and wait for my fate to be decided.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I pray you truly are prepared, Lord Phainon.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You seem worried.
You spoke to him?
I spoke at length with Lord Phainon before. There was hesitation in his words.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes, there was hesitation in his words.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The manifestation of the prophecy must have seen this. It saw Lord Phainon's heart wavering.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Looks like she fell asleep. Presiding over this ritual must take quite a toll.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If he can conquer his fear and return as a demigod, we will be one step closer to the miracle that the prophecy promised.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You have a lot of faith in him.
What if he fails?
...That would mean his time hasn't come yet. And that there is a more arduous mission for him to see through.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You must have noticed by now. Every Chrysos Heir here bears... a flaw of sorts. Be it the curse of immortality, or the constant erosion of their humanity, or...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But not Phainon. He is a Chrysos Heir without flaw, a perfect vessel for divinity.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Still too late, huh...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Within Amphoreus, at [Trailblazer]'s private bath chamber...
The constellation of the {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Lance of Fury{RUBY_E#} is already illuminated. That must mean...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The Coreflame has been surrendered, but Lord Phainon's test isn't over yet.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hmm... but come to think of it, I don't remember when the last time I ate something was...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Hmm? But come to think of it... I don't remember when the last time I ate something was...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The prophecy sent an ambassador. They acknowledged Lord Phainon's strength and character, but had doubts about his strength of will.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: He must conquer his fear and prove himself to the prophecy.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I was right to be worried.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I want to formally thank you, outsiders. Were it not for your aid, our campaign against {RUBY_B#Strife Titan}Nikador{RUBY_E#} would have been a hundred times more arduous.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Mydei, what do you mean when you said you were "worried"?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: They don't know yet?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That guy... has always been tormented by his past.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I may not be the right person to tell you about him, but you must know his past if you are to continue fighting alongside Phainon.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Kremnoans revere strength and military might, but that does not mean we lack etiquette.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Lord Mydei... please allow me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hm... Very well.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Before he was chosen by the prophecy, Lord Phainon had everything taken away from him: His home, his family, his close friends... Everything he once swore to protect.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: He became a hollowed shell in his youth, and the blazing flames of vengeance were the only thing sustaining him.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The prophecy gave him a new mission, granting him a new life as a Chrysos Heir. But which is more important to him: His new mission or his desire for revenge?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm afraid only he knows... No, perhaps he himself is still struggling to get to an answer.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I acknowledge his strength, but... fear is something not even the sharpest of swords can cut through.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I hope you've toughened your resolve, Deliverer...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Only a will as tough as stone can shatter the darkest nightmares.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Is something wrong?
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Ugh, don't keep me in suspense. Come on, tell me already. What did you see?
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Haha, I just wanted to get a reaction out of you. Alright, I'll tell you.
Some system hours ago, aboard the Astral Express...
...This card is the Deliverer.
Deliverer...? What does that mean?
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Uh... The interpretation is really long. Maybe I should just skip it.

All you need to know is, this card means... you'll be a hero worshiped by all! You will protect this world and save lots and lots of people from scary enemies with your sword! Do you like the sound of that?
But...
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: What's the matter? This is a good card!
But I don't want to be everyone's hero! I just want to stay in this village with everyone I know.
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Grandpa and grandma said the outside world is full of bad people. That's why they're always at war... Who wants to save bad people like them! I can be a hero, but only our village's little hero!
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Haha...
Well, little hero... If the day comes for us to say goodbye to Aedes Elysiae, could you become a Deliverer then?
Do I... have to leave the village?
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Mm-hmm. If something like that happens, someone will have to save the world.
Then... Then I'll...
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Haha, I'm just teasing you. Don't worry. Aedes Elysiae is a peaceful place. Bad people won't reach us here.
Are you going home already...? If you're not in a hurry, should we go play with the fairies again?
Fairies! Okay! I love playing with them! Hmph, I'll win back the wooden sword I lost to them!
rows.speaker: Young Phainon

rows.text: Heehee! Look at how excited that got you. Let's go then.
May this world never have need for a Deliverer.
Pom-Pom, have you prepared our meals already?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course, the food's ready! March isn't feeling well, so Pom-Pom has specially prepared the conductor's special bland meal that'll be easy on her stomach.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Can you bring it to her, Himeko?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Gladly. Why don't we also get her a—
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Nuh-uh! No coffee when she's already feeling unwell!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Heh... I guess you're right.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: March? I'm coming in, okay?
rows.speaker: Himeko
